words.gloss: you do not maintain or realize the sulking

literal: Having mingled and appeasing lover if you see, having sulked you do not realize; false anger you show, my heart!
translation: O my heart! If you see our lover who comes to embrace and appease us, you forget to remain sulky; yet, in his absence, you show only a false anger.
modern: கூடி அணைத்துத் தன் அன்பைப் புரியவைக்கும் காதலரைக் கண்டால், நீ ஊடல் கொள்வதை மறந்துவிடுகிறாய்; என் நெஞ்சமே! இப்போது மட்டும் அவரிடம் வீணாகப் பொய்க் கோபம் கொள்கிறாய்.
explanation: In this couplet, the heroine speaks to her own heart, pointing out its inconsistency. She notes that when her lover is present, ready to embrace and comfort her, her heart completely forgets its resolve to remain sulky ('pulantu uṇarāy'). However, in his absence, the heart pretends to be angry and vows to show resentment. Thus, she chides her heart for harboring a 'false anger' ('poykkāyvu') that vanishes the moment the lover appears.
